## [CN]规则
## [EN]Rules

| 中文 | English |
|:---|:---|
| 见右列。 | **Language version**: Swift 5.9 syntax that builds with the Swift 6 toolchain of Xcode 27; minimum deployment target as in the podspec (iOS 13 for the library). Gate newer APIs with `if #available` / `@available`, never with OS version strings. |
| | **Objective-C compatibility of the library**: public types inherit from `NSObject` (or a UIKit class) and are `@objc(CYLName)` with the old Objective-C name; members that Objective-C callers use are `@objc(oldSelector:)` so the selector does not change. Keep `CYL` prefixes on Objective-C names and `cyl_` on category members (Swift extensions of UIKit types keep `@objc(cyl_name)`). Do not rename public API; add a new name and deprecate the old one when a rename is needed. |
| | **Enums and protocols used by Objective-C headers stay Objective-C** until those headers are Swift too: Swift reads the remaining Objective-C public headers without the generated Swift interface, so they can refer to a Swift class (`@class`) but not to a Swift enum or protocol ([Swift-Migration.md](Swift-Migration.md), step 8). |
| | **Keep the Swift names callers already use**: Clang imported every Objective-C method into Swift under a name, often shortened (it drops a trailing word that repeats the return or parameter type: `-cyl_getViewControllerInsteadOfNavigationController` is `cyl_getViewControllerInsteadOfNavigation()` in Swift), or set by `NS_SWIFT_NAME`. A translated member keeps that Swift name and the old selector: `@objc(cyl_getViewControllerInsteadOfNavigationController) public func cyl_getViewControllerInsteadOfNavigation()`. Check the name in the generated Swift interface of the old header or in Swift callers (`grep` the examples) before translating. |
| | **Kept names and SonarCloud** (added 2026-11-12): names that must stay for compatibility (`cyl_` category members, `CYL` C functions and constants with their Objective-C names) break SonarCloud's Swift naming rules `swift:S100` / `swift:S115`. SonarCloud's Swift analyzer does not support `// NOSONAR`, and automatic analysis ignores `sonar.issue.ignore.*`, so these findings are marked **Accept** in the SonarCloud UI by the maintainer (bulk change, filtered by rule and file). Never accept a name that is free to change: private and internal helpers, and the Swift-side names of `@_cdecl` entry points, use lowerCamelCase (`cylImageNamedEntryPoint`).
| 本条按用户要求使用英文（见右列）。 | **TODO (2026-11-22, chenyilong-0b, branch `feat/cross-platform-components`, PR #788): re-evaluate the `CYL` / `cyl_` prefixes for Swift, guided by the static analysis.** Queued behind the animation engine migration (docs/Swift-Migration.md, row of 2026-11-21), which was started first (tasks run in the order they were given). Prompt (verbatim): "找到本项目instructions 相关文件以及skills相关文件，如果没有就新增文件保证写入成功，全英文写入： 根据github pr评论区的静态分析报告， 重新评估 instructions 中关于cyl_ CYL 方法名前缀名，类名前缀名的必要性， 这个前缀目的主要是为了在objc项目中， 兼容分类方法可能覆盖其他同名实现的场景， 以及弥补objc没有命名空间导致类名冲突的问题，请在Swift上重新评估该前缀必要性， 以及其他有相关机制，能保证我们的库不会导致类名冲突， 方法名冲突的其他语言， 以静态分析为指导意见， 重新调整代码命名， 以适应静态分析建议". English: find this project's instructions and skills files (create them if missing, so the write succeeds) and write in English only: from the static analysis report in the GitHub PR comments, re-evaluate the instructions' rule on the `cyl_` / `CYL` prefixes of method and class names. The prefixes exist for Objective-C: a category method can override another implementation with the same name, and Objective-C has no namespaces, so class names can collide. Re-evaluate whether Swift needs them, and the same for the other languages whose own mechanisms already prevent class and method name collisions; let the static analysis guide the naming and rename the code to follow its advice. Facts found (SonarCloud, PR #788, 2026-11-22): 919 open naming findings: `swift:S100` 651 on `cyl_` members and 77 on `CYL` functions, `swift:S115` 144 on `CYL` constants, `swift:S116` 16, `swift:S117` 11, `swift:S101` 3 (`_CYL…` types), 14 on `cylflatdesign_…`; most in `CYLConstants+Keys.swift` (112), `CYLConstantsFunctions.swift` (55), the badge and `UIView` / `UIViewController` extensions. Mechanisms to weigh: Swift types are namespaced by module (no prefix needed for Swift-only types), but the Objective-C runtime still has one flat class and selector namespace for everything `@objc` (an `@objc` extension member on a UIKit class can collide like a category method), so `@objc(cyl_name)` / `@objc(CYLName)` stay while the Swift spelling can drop the underscore (`cylName`, or no prefix where the module and the type already scope it); Kotlin / Java (packages), Dart (libraries, import prefixes), TypeScript / JavaScript (ES modules) and ArkTS (modules) have namespaces, except for extension functions on platform types and global names. Constraint: the public API rule (never remove or change a shipped API). Decision on shipped names (owner-approved 2026-11-22, relayed by the CYLSearchViewController session with its `cyl-naming` skill; the same scheme as CYLTableViewPlaceHolder's docs/Swift-Naming.md): rename the Swift name, keep the Objective-C name through `@objc(cyl_oldName)`, and keep the old Swift name for one release as an `@available(*, deprecated, renamed: "newName")` forward; only those forwards may stay flagged, listed for the owner to accept in SonarCloud (`// NOSONAR` does not work in Swift). The rule text is drafted on PR #823 (`.agents/skills/cyl-naming/SKILL.md`, AGENTS.md); bring it to this branch with the rename. Rubric: **100** = the prefix rule rewritten per language in AGENTS.md, the instructions files and the `cyl-*` skills (English); every free-to-rename name (internal, private, new on this branch, `@_cdecl` Swift sides, C-style constants as Swift members) renamed to the analyzers' patterns with the Objective-C names kept through `@objc(...)`; shipped names handled as the maintainer decides; unit tests, both pod lints, the demos and SwiftPM build; SonarCloud naming findings on PR #788 down to the accepted kept names only. **60** = the rule re-evaluated and written in every instructions and skills file, and the internal / private / branch-new names renamed with the same checks. **Status (2026-11-22): the rename of internal and private names is under way, see "Sonar naming rename" below.** **Update (2026-11-23): DONE for Swift** (buckets a to d, decision B, 85 / 100); remaining: the rule text in `AGENTS.md` / the instructions / the `cyl-*` skills (PR #823) and the SonarCloud re-scan of PR #788. |
| | **Names**: Swift API Design Guidelines: clarity at the point of use, argument labels that read as phrases, `is`/`has` for Booleans, no abbreviations except well-known ones (`URL`, `ID`). Types are `UpperCamelCase`, everything else `lowerCamelCase`. |
| | **Types**: `let` by default; value types for data that has no identity; `final` for classes that are not meant to be subclassed (not for public classes that apps subclass, such as `CYLPlusButton`). Prefer `guard` for early exits; no force unwrapping (`!`) or `try!` in library code, except for `IBOutlet`-style invariants documented in a comment. |
| | **Associated objects** (state of category-style extensions): one private `static var` key per value (`UInt8` address), accessed through `objc_getAssociatedObject` / `objc_setAssociatedObject` in a computed property. |
| | **Concurrency**: UI code is `@MainActor`; library entry points used from Objective-C stay synchronous on the main thread as before. No unstructured `Task` in the library without a comment that says who cancels it. |
| | **Errors**: Swift `throws` for new Swift-only API; `NSError **` style (`throws` exposed to Objective-C) where an Objective-C method returned `NSError`. |
| | **Comments**: every public declaration has a documentation comment in the three-line `/** … */` block form (`/**`, ` * [EN] …`, ` * [CN] …`, ` */`), bilingual as the rest of the library ([Public API comment format] in `AGENTS.md`); no `///` in library files. `// FIX: issue #N` notes move with the code they explain. |
| | **Formatting**: 4 spaces, lines up to 120 characters, one type per file named after it (extensions: `UIView+CYLName.swift`), `// MARK: -` sections, trailing closures only for the last closure argument. |
| | **Translation from Objective-C**: keep behavior identical (including nil handling of the old code and the order of side effects); translate tests' expectations, not the tests themselves; one file per commit when a file is large, each commit with a clean build, the unit tests and the migration score. |
| | **Examples bend, the core does not (added 2026-11-13)**: when the Swift migration breaks an example's build, fix the example first. Every example (Objective-C, Swift, SwiftUI, React Native, Flutter, and the other demos) has the lowest priority: change its code freely, and do not keep anything in the core layer only so that an example keeps compiling unchanged. Keep the core Swift code free of baggage: no workaround, extra overload, kept name or compatibility shim exists only because of how an example uses it. This document decides. Compatibility for apps still counts: the public API rule (no removed or renamed public API) and the kept Objective-C selectors stay, because they protect apps, not examples. |

Scheme: types keep `CYL`; members of our own types lose the prefix (`cyl_foo` to `foo`, or `cylFoo` when `foo` would clash); members added in extensions of system types become `cylFoo`; constants and globals become lowerCamelCase or static members; locals and parameters lowerCamelCase. Bucket a: private / fileprivate / internal and not visible to Objective-C, renamed freely. Bucket b: internal but visible to the Objective-C runtime, renamed with an explicit `@objc(oldSelector)`. Buckets c and d (public and open names) are NOT part of this run (the owner has not decided on forwards). | | **Decision B (owner, 2026-11-22): rename, keep a deprecated forward.** Public names are renamed to the analyzers' lowerCamelCase patterns; every old public Swift name stays as a deprecated Swift-only forward in a separate file under a folder named `Deprecated/`, and those folders are excluded from SonarCloud analysis (`sonar.exclusions` in `.sonarcloud.properties`). The forwards are removed at the next major version. Rule for a renamed member: the new declaration keeps the exact Objective-C name through an explicit `@objc(oldSelector)` where the member is visible to Objective-C (the selector dump stays identical) and keeps its documentation comment; the old Swift name is re-declared in `Deprecated/` as `@available(*, deprecated, renamed: "newName(label:)") @nonobjc public func oldName(...) -> R { newName(...) }` (no `@objc` on a forward, properties forward `get` / `set`, constants forward `public let CYLX = cylX`), with a short bilingual doc block. New names: members added to extensions (of system types and of our types) become `cylFoo`; members of our own types lose the prefix when the plain name is free (`reloadTabButtons`); global functions and constants become `cylFoo` (`CYLScreenWidth()` to `cylScreenWidth()`, `CYLTabBarItemTitle` to `cylTabBarItemTitle`, `Notification.Name.CYLTabBarLoginStateDidChange` to `.cylTabBarLoginStateDidChange`); `@_cdecl("…")` C names never change. Name clashes: a global constant whose new name equals a member function name is hidden inside that type, so the internal member is renamed (`cylTabBarItemTitleColorValue()`, `cylTabBarContentView()`, `cylHandleFlatDesignTabBarItemDidChange(_:)`), or, where the member is public API, the constant gets the suffix `Value` (`cylPlusButtonWidthValue`); twelve `@nonobjc` wrappers whose `cylFoo` twin already existed became the forward of that twin. Call sites in the library, tests, examples, `README.md` and the Swift samples of `docs/` use the new names, so no deprecation warning remains. The folders: `CYLTabBarController/Swift/Deprecated/`, `CYLTabBarController/CYLBadgeView/Swift/Deprecated/`, `CYLTabBarController/CYLUtils/Swift/Deprecated/`, `CYLTabBarController/CYLFlatDesignTabBar/CYLFlatDesignTabBar-ObjectiveC/Swift/Deprecated/` (43 files, one per extended type or source file, named `<Type>+<Area>DeprecatedNames.swift`; the area keeps the file names unique, because Swift rejects two files with the same name in a module). Build systems: the CocoaPods `Core` subspec lists `Swift/Deprecated/*.swift` explicitly (`Swift/*.swift` is not recursive), the other subspecs use `**` globs, SwiftPM reads whole folders, the Xcode project has the 43 files in four `Deprecated` groups and in the framework target. |
